questions.stem: What of the following is true about plasma half-life?

options.label: B
options.text: It is directly proportional to clearance

options.label: C
options.text: It is inversely proportional to volume of distribution

options.label: D
options.text: It is constant for the drugs eliminated by first order kinetics

questions.answerText: It is constant for the drugs eliminated by first order kinetics
questions.solutionHtml:
drugs eliminated by first order kinetics.

 

Explanation:

 

Option A. Is the same as bioavailability:

 

This statement is incorrect. Bioavailability refers to the fraction of an administered dose of a drug that reaches the systemic circulation in its active form. In contrast, plasma half-life is the time required for the concentration of the drug in the plasma to reduce to half its original value. These are distinct pharmacokinetic properties.

 

Option B. It is directly proportional to clearance:

 

This is incorrect. Plasma half-life is inversely related to clearance. Clearance is the rate at which a drug is removed from the body. If a drug is cleared quickly from the body (high clearance), its plasma half-life will be shorter, and vice versa.

 

Option C. It is inversely proportional to volume of distribution:

 

This statement is actually a misunderstanding. Plasma half-life is not solely dependent on the volume of distribution. The relationship between half-life, volume of distribution, and clearance is given by the formula: half-life = (0.693 × volume of distribution) / clearance. Thus, half-life is directly proportional to the volume of distribution and inversely proportional to clearance. 


Educational Objective:

 

For drugs eliminated via first-order kinetics, the plasma half-life remains constant because a fixed percentage of the drug is metabolized per unit time, regardless of the drug's concentration in the plasma.



ore, the correct answer is: It is constant for the drugs eliminated by first order kinetics.

questions.stem: While reviewing the pharmacology of various medications, a medical student notes that drug-protein interactions can significantly influence the pharmacokinetics and effects of medications. Which of the following statements regarding drug-protein binding in the plasma is incorrect?

options.label: A
options.text: Acidic drugs bind to albumin in plasma

options.label: B
options.text: Basic drugs bind to alpha-1 acid glycoprotein in plasma

options.label: C
options.text: Drugs having higher affinity for a plasma protein can displace the other drug from the same protein

options.label: D
options.text: Sex steroid hormones do not bind to any protein in plasma

questions.answerText: Sex steroid hormones do not bind to any protein in plasma
questions.solutionHtml:
/span>

 

Explanation:

 

Option A. Acidic drugs bind to albumin in plasma. This statement is correct. Acidic drugs often bind to albumin, which is the main protein in human blood plasma. Albumin carries a negative charge and can bind to various acidic drugs, affecting their distribution and availability in the body.

 

Option B. Basic drugs bind to alpha-1 acid glycoprotein in plasma. This statement is also correct. Alpha-1 acid glycoprotein is a plasma protein that primarily binds to basic (positively charged) drugs. The binding affinity of drugs to this protein can influence their pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics.

 

Option C. Drugs having higher affinity for a plasma protein can displace the other drug from the same protein. This statement is correct. If two drugs bind to the same plasma protein (like albumin) and one has a higher affinity for the protein, it can displace the other. This displacement can increase the concentration of the free (unbound) form of the displaced drug, potentially leading to increased activity or toxicity.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Sex steroid hormones do bind to plasma proteins, specifically to Sex Hormone Binding Globulin (SHBG) and albumin, which can influence their bioavailability and action in the body.

questions.stem: A 32-year-old male is brought to the emergency department after ingesting an overdose of a medication. In order to enhance drug clearance, you consider the modification of urinary pH as a therapeutic measure. Knowing that manipulating the urinary pH can increase the excretion of certain drugs by altering their ionization state, which of the following drugs would not have its excretion increased by alkalinization of the urine?
questions.solutionHtml:
ng>Acidifying the urine would increase morphine excretion.

 

Explanation:

 

Option A. Aspirin: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is an acidic drug. Alkalinizing the urine with agents such as sodium bicarbonate can enhance its ionization and excretion.

 

Option B. Methotrexate: This is also an acidic drug, and alkalinization of the urine will increase its ionization, decreasing reabsorption and increasing elimination.

Educational Objective:

 

In cases of drug overdose, urinary alkalinization is utilized to increase the excretion of acidic drugs by enhancing their ionization, which does not apply to basic drugs like morphine that are better excreted in acidic conditions. Remember, the drugs ending with ‘ine’ are basic.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old farm worker is rushed to a nearby emergency department after an accidental exposure to parathion. Which of the following drugs can be given to increase the activity of his acetyl cholinesterase?

:justify"> 

Explanation:

 

Option A. Atropine: Atropine is drug of choice as an antidote in organophosphate poisoning, but it does not increase the activity of acetylcholinesterase. Instead, it serves to counteract the effects of excess acetylcholine on muscarinic receptors, thereby relieving symptoms such as bradycardia, salivation, and bronchoconstriction. Atropine does not affect the nicotinic receptor-mediated effects (e.g., muscle weakness, paralysis).

Therefore, it is not used in the treatment of organophosphate poisoning and is contraindicated in such cases.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Pralidoxime is used to reactivate acetylcholinesterase inhibited by organophosphates, thereby reducing the toxic accumulation of acetylcholine. questions.stem: A 7-year-old child opened his father’s drawer and ingested multiple tablets of his cardiac medication, metoprolol. The child was brought to hospital with profound hypotension and bradycardia. What is the specific antidote used in this situation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Glucagon

 

The case described is indicative of beta-blocker poisoning due to the ingestion of metoprolol. Glucagon is the specific antidote for beta-blocker toxicity. 

 

Metoprolol is a beta-blocker that slows down the heart rate and reduces the strength of the heart's contractions. In an overdose, it can cause bradycardia and hypotension. Normally beta-blockers work by blocking beta-adrenergic receptors on heart cells. These receptors usually respond to adrenaline and similar substances to increase heart rate and strength. In an overdose, the heart can't respond to adrenaline because the beta-blockers are blocking the receptors too much. This makes it hard to use medications like adrenaline or dobutamine effectively. Glucagon bypasses the blocked receptors. Instead of working through the beta-adrenergic receptors, it stimulates glucagon receptors in heart and increases cyclic AMP (cAMP). Latter helps the heart cells to increase their rate and strength of contraction. This means the heart can beat faster and pump blood more effectively, even when beta-blockers are blocking the usual pathways. Thus,by increasing cAMP, glucagon helps counteract the effects of the beta-blocker overdose, improving heart rate and blood pressure, and stabilizing the patient's condition.

 

In summary, glucagon works as an antidote for beta-blocker overdose by increasing cAMP in heart cells, which helps the heart beat faster and stronger, even when the usual beta-adrenergic receptors are blocked by the overdose.

 

Treatment for Beta-Blocker Poisoning:

 

  • Glucagon is used due to its ability to stimulate cardiac activity without relying on beta-adrenergic receptors.
  • Atropine may be administered if there is severe bradycardia, and a pacemaker may be necessary.
  • Calcium gluconate can also be beneficial in treating beta-blocker poisoning.
  • In cases of hypotension, large doses of isoproterenol or an alpha receptor agonist may be required.

 

Other Options

 

Option A. Dobutamine:

 

Dobutamine is a beta-1 adrenergic agonist that can increase heart rate and contractility. While it can be used to support cardiac function, it is not the specific antidote for beta-blocker overdose. Its effectiveness may also be reduced due to the beta-blockade.

 

Option C.  Adrenaline:

 

Adrenaline (epinephrine) is a non-selective adrenergic agonist that can increase heart rate and blood pressure. It can be used in severe cases of beta-blocker overdose, but it is not the specific antidote. Its use may be limited by the beta-blockade, and it can have significant side effects.

 

Option D. Nor-adrenaline:

 

Nor-adrenaline (norepinephrine) is primarily an alpha-adrenergic agonist with some beta-adrenergic effects. It is used to increase blood pressure through vasoconstriction. However, it is not the specific antidote for beta-blocker overdose and may not adequately address bradycardia.

 

Educational Objective

 

In cases of beta-blocker overdose, such as with metoprolol, the specific antidote is glucagon. It works by increasing cyclic AMP independently of the beta-adrenergic receptors, thereby improving heart rate and contractility despite the beta-blockade. Understanding the role of glucagon and its mechanism of action is crucial in managing beta-blocker toxicity effectively.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old man came with urinary symptoms of increased frequency and hesitation. The patient was diagnosed with benign hyperplasia of prostate. Which of the drugs will help to prevent further growth and possibly reduces the size of the prostate?

For a patient diagnosed with BPH, finasteride is the drug of choice to not only alleviate urinary symptoms but also potentially reduce prostate size due to its mechanism of inhibiting the enzyme 5-alpha reductase and lowering intraprostatic DHT levels.

In a patient with hypothyroidism indicated by symptoms of thyroid hormone deficiency and elevated TSH levels with normal T4, L-Thyroxine is the appropriate treatment to normalize thyroid function and alleviate symptoms.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an adverse effect of dapagliflozin?

options.label: C
options.text: Increased incidence of urinary tract infections

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. All the above

 

Option D:

 

  • Dapagliflozin is an SGLT-2 inhibitor used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus.
  • Glucose is freely filtered by the renal glomeruli. Sodium-glucose transporter 2 (SGLT2) accounts for 90% of glucose reabsorption, and its inhibition causes glycosuria and lowers glucose levels in patients with type 2 diabetes.
  • SGLT2 inhibitors lower glucose levels by changing the renal threshold and not by insulin action.
  • Due to increased excretion of glucose in the urine, dapagliflozin increases the risk of UTI. Further, there is polyuria and weight loss with the use of this drug.
  • Other adverse effects of SGLT2 inhibitors include ketoacidosis, urosepsis, Fournier's gangrene, and increased incidence of UTI and genital tract infections.

 

Educational objective:


Dapagliflozin and other SGLT2 inhibitors are effective in lowering blood glucose levels in type 2 diabetes patients but can lead to several adverse effects such as weight loss, polyuria, and an increased risk of UTIs. Patients and healthcare providers should be aware of these potential side effects and manage them through regular monitoring and supportive care.

options.label: D
options.text: Vigabatrin is a GABA transacetylase inhibitor.

bri,sans-serif">Explanation:

Vigabatrin effectively treats seizures by inhibiting GABA transaminase, thereby increasing the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA in the brain, crucial for reducing excessive neuronal firing associated with epilepsy. ore they are relatively safer in elderly patients and in those with liver disease. Thus, Lorazepam (option C) is a benzodiazepine that is preferred for managing alcohol withdrawal symptoms in patients with liver disease. It undergoes glucuronidation rather than oxidation. questions.stem: A patient with bipolar disorder was treated with lithium. Hydrochlorothiazide was prescribed for his hypertension. He developed nausea, vomiting, coarse tremors and brisk reflexes 2 weeks after taking drugs. What is the likely reason for this presentation?

options.label: B
options.text: Decreased metabolism of hydrochlorothiazide by lithium.

options.label: C
options.text: Increased renal tubular reabsorption of lithium.

options.label: D
options.text: Thiazide acts as an add on drug to lithium.

questions.answerText: Increased renal tubular reabsorption of lithium.
questions.solutionHtml:
Other Options:

 

Option A. Side effects of hydrochlorothiazide: While hydrochlorothiazide can cause side effects like electrolyte imbalances and dehydration, its common side effects do not typically include the combination of symptoms seen in lithium toxicity (nausea, vomiting, coarse tremors, and brisk reflexes). These symptoms are more specifically indicative of lithium toxicity rather than direct side effects of hydrochlorothiazide.
 

Option B. Decreased metabolism of hydrochlorothiazide by lithium: Lithium does not significantly impact the metabolism of hydrochlorothiazide. The metabolism and clearance of hydrochlorothiazide are primarily renal and are not substantially altered by concurrent lithium use, making this option an unlikely cause of the patient's symptoms.
 

Option D. Thiazide acts as an add-on drug to lithium: There is no evidence to suggest that thiazide diuretics act as add-on drugs to enhance the therapeutic effects of lithium in the treatment of bipolar disorder. The interaction between hydrochlorothiazide and lithium that is of clinical significance relates to the effect on lithium's renal handling, rather than a synergistic effect on mood stabilization.
 

Educational Objective:

 

The key learning point from this scenario is understanding the pharmacological interaction between lithium and thiazide diuretics, such as hydrochlorothiazide, and how this interaction can lead to increased serum lithium levels and subsequent lithium toxicity.



lexes, is increased renal tubular reabsorption of lithium. When hydrochlorothiazide, a thiazide diuretic, is administered alongside lithium, it can lead to decreased renal clearance of lithium by increasing its reabsorption in the renal tubules. This pharmacological interaction results in elevated serum lithium levels, potentially culminating in lithium toxicity. The symptoms of lithium toxicity closely align with those experienced by the patient, making this option the most plausible explanation for the clinical presentation observed.

questions.solutionHtml:
span>

 

Explanation:

 

The false statement about clozapine is option B, which states that "Blood level below 350 ng/ml should be maintained to avoid agranulocytosis." This statement is not true because there is no specific blood level of clozapine that is associated with the risk of agranulocytosis, which is dose-independent adverse effect of clozapine. High plasma concentration of Clozapine increases the risk of seizures (dose-dependent). However, the usual plasma concentration required in many people is 300-600 ng/ml.

  • Clozapine is an atypical antipsychotic drug that has high potency to block 5HT2 receptors as compared to D2 receptors. However, it also blocks D4 receptors, muscarinic receptors, alpha receptors and H1 receptors.
  • It suppresses both positive as well as negative symptoms of schizophrenia. It is the first FDA approved drug for anti-suicide indication.
  • It is used only as a reserve drug due to the risk of precipitation of seizures (even in non-epileptics) and agranulocytosis. Convulsions are dose-dependent adverse effects seen only at higher doses whereas agranulocytosis is independent of dose.
  • Clozapine should be started at low doses (12.5 mg) and gradually dose should be increased. Baseline WBC counts should be measured, and then weekly counts should be done at least for the first 6 months. When WBC count becomes less than 3000/mm3 or absolute neutrophil count becomes less than 1500/mm3, Clozapine should be discontinued. After discontinuation, weekly WBC counts should be measured for an additional 4 weeks.
  • It should not be used with Carbamazepine due to two reasons:
    • Carbamazepine induces its metabolism and thus decreases plasma concentration.
    • Carbamazepine has bone marrow suppressant action and can add to agranulocytosis caused by Clozapine.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not an adverse effect of salbutamol?
questions.solutionHtml:
ation:

questions.stem: Which of the following antimalarial drug has gametocidal action against all species of Plasmodia?
questions.solutionHtml:

Option A. Quinine: While quinine has some activity against the gametocytes of P. vivax, it does not have broad gametocidal activity against all Plasmodium species, especially not against P. falciparum gametocytes.

 

Option B. Chloroquine: Similar to quinine, chloroquine is effective against P. vivax gametocytes but lacks gametocidal activity against all species, particularly failing against P. falciparum.

 

Option D. Artesunate: Although artesunate is a very effective antimalarial, especially for the treatment of severe malaria, it does not have inherent gametocidal properties against Plasmodium species. However, it can enhance the gametocidal effects of other drugs when used in combination.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Primaquine is the only antimalarial drug listed that has the capability to exert gametocidal action against all species of Plasmodium. This makes it a vital component of the malaria eradication strategy, particularly in efforts aimed at preventing the transmission of the disease.

 

When treating malaria, particularly P. vivax or P. ovale, primaquine is used to ensure the clearance of liver stages and to prevent relapse, highlighting its critical role in comprehensive malaria treatment protocols.

questions.stem: During the investigation for an outbreak of MRSA in the hospital, it was found that a nurse of NICU had MRSA colonization of anterior nares. What is the best treatment for her?
questions.solutionHtml:
style="font-size:12pt">Option B. Oral Vancomycin: Incorrect. Oral vancomycin is not absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract and thus is ineffective for treating MRSA colonization of the nares. It is used primarily to treat colitis caused by Clostridium difficile.

 

Option C. Inhaled colistin: Incorrect. Colistin is used to treat infections caused by certain multi-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, typically in the lungs (e.g., for cystic fibrosis patients), and is not suitable for decolonization of MRSA in the nares.

 

Option D. IV cefazolin: Incorrect. Cefazolin is ineffective against MRSA due to the bacterium’s resistance mechanisms, and it is typically not used for nasal decolonization.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Topical Mupirocin is the first-line treatment for decolonization of MRSA in the anterior nares, especially in healthcare workers or patients where MRSA carriage poses a significant risk of infection transmission. This measure is part of infection control protocols to minimize the spread of MRSA in healthcare facilities.

questions.stem: Antimicrobial resistance to which of the following drugs develop by synthesis of inactivating enzymes? Aminoglycosides Beta lactams Chloramphenicol Fluoroquinolones
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. I, II and III

 

Option A:

 

Antimicrobial resistance through the synthesis of inactivating enzymes is a major mechanism by which bacteria evade the effects of antibiotics. These enzymes chemically modify the drug molecule, rendering it inactive against the bacteria.

 

  • Aminoglycosides: Resistance occurs via enzymes that modify the drug, typically by phosphorylation, adenylylation, or acetylation.
  • Beta lactams: Enzymes such as beta-lactamases cleave the beta-lactam ring, deactivating the drug’s antibacterial activity.
  • Chloramphenicol: Enzymatic inactivation occurs via acetylation, which prevents the drug from binding to the bacterial ribosome.

 

Fluoroquinolones (IV) are not typically inactivated by enzymes; instead, resistance often develops through mutations that alter drug targets or increase drug efflux.

 

Educational Objective:

questions.stem: Tafenoquine is a recently approved new drug. It is indicated for?
questions.solutionHtml:
Option B. Prophylaxis of malaria in pregnancy: This is not an indication for tafenoquine, as it can cause hemolysis in patients with G-6-PD deficiency, a condition that cannot be ruled out in the fetus, making it contraindicated during pregnancy.

 

Option C. Treatment of severe falciparum malaria: Tafenoquine is not indicated for the treatment of severe falciparum malaria, where other medications such as intravenous artesunate are the treatments of choice.

 

Option D. Treatment in children < 2 years: The drug is not approved for use in children under the age of 16 due to the lack of safety data and the risk of hemolysis, especially in those with G-6-PD deficiency.

 

Educational objective:

 

Tafenoquine is a valuable addition to the antimalarial arsenal, especially for the radical cure of P. vivax, which is notorious for causing relapses. However, it must be used cautiously considering its contraindications, including G-6-PD deficiency, pregnancy, and age restrictions.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old child is started on chemotherapy. One of the medications used in the treatment is L-asparaginase. This drug works by depleting asparagine, an amino acid that is required for the growth and survival of leukemia cells. Which of the following cancers is L-asparaginase commonly used to treat?
questions.solutionHtml:
y">Option B. Acute Myeloblastic Leukemia (AML): AML is another type of leukemia but primarily affects different lineages of cells within the bone marrow. L-asparaginase is not typically used in the treatment of AML.

 

Option C. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL): CLL progresses more slowly than ALL and generally affects older adults. It is not treated with L-asparaginase.

 

Option D. Chronic Myelocytic Leukemia (CML): CML is a chronic form of leukemia affecting primarily adults. L-asparaginase is not effective against CML cells as they do not rely on external sources of asparagine like ALL cells.

 

Educational Objective:

 

L-asparaginase is particularly significant in the treatment of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) due to its unique mechanism of depleting asparagine, which is essential for the survival of ALL cells. This makes it a key component of chemotherapy regimens for ALL, especially in pediatric patients, where it can be combined with other drugs to enhance treatment efficacy and manage the disease effectively.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements best describes the mechanism of action of basiliximab?

options.label: A
options.text: Basiliximab directly inhibits the proliferation of T-cells

options.label: B
options.text: Basiliximab promotes the activation of B-cells

options.label: C
options.text: Basiliximab blocks the binding of interleukin-2 (IL-2) to its receptor on activated T-cells

options.label: D
options.text: Basiliximab enhances the differentiation of dendritic cells

questions.answerText: Basiliximab blocks the binding of interleukin-2 (IL-2) to its receptor on activated T-cells
questions.solutionHtml:
;

Option A. Basiliximab directly inhibits the proliferation of T-cells: Incorrect. because basiliximab itself does not directly inhibit cell proliferation; instead, it prevents IL-2 from activating T-cells, which indirectly inhibits their proliferation.

 

Option B. Basiliximab promotes the activation of B-cells: Incorrect. Basiliximab’s action is specific to T-cells and does not involve direct effects on B-cell activation.

 

Option D. Basiliximab enhances the differentiation of dendritic cells: Incorrect. Basiliximab's mechanism of action is centered on T-cells and does not affect the differentiation of dendritic cells.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Basiliximab serves as an immunosuppressant by specifically blocking the IL-2 receptor on activated T-cells, thereby preventing their activation and proliferation. This selective inhibition is critical in preventing organ rejection following transplantation, making basiliximab a valuable therapeutic tool in transplant medicine.

questions.stem: Pulmonary fibrosis is an adverse effect of which of the following anti-cancer drugs?
questions.solutionHtml:
trong>Explanation:

 

Option A. Mitomycin C: This is an alkylating agent used in cancer chemotherapy. Its common side effects include bone marrow suppression, nausea, vomiting, and renal toxicity, but it is not primarily known for causing pulmonary fibrosis.

 

Option B. Hydroxyurea: This medication is used for various myeloproliferative disorders and sickle cell disease. Its side effects often include bone marrow suppression and gastrointestinal symptoms, but it is not typically associated with pulmonary fibrosis.

 

Option D. Cisplatin: A platinum-containing chemotherapy drug used to treat various types of cancers. While nephrotoxicity (kidney damage) and ototoxicity (hearing damage) are common adverse effects, it is not typically associated with pulmonary fibrosis.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Bleomycin is known to cause pulmonary fibrosis, which is a condition characterized by the scarring and thickening of lung tissue.
